LHX.sentence: L3Harris is basically flat, but the thing worth knowing is that it now trades at a premium to the other big defense companies rather than its usual discount, so the easy bargain in the stock has mostly played out even though defense spending keeps supporting the business.

ASML.sentence: ASML has drifted down about 12% from its high and is having a soft stretch, but nothing has changed about the fact that they're the only company in the world making a certain essential chipmaking machine.

LIN.sentence: Linde is having a quiet, steady week — they supply industrial gases on long-term contracts and nudge prices up a little each year, which is the whole story with this one.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft is quiet — it slipped a little but has held up far better than the other big tech names this month, with the Azure cloud and AI story grinding along without any drama.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher is down slightly as the lab-supply business works through its slowest stretch, with customers finishing off stockpiles they'd built up — the thing to watch is whether orders start picking back up from here.

CVX.sentence: Chevron slipped a bit today, which is mostly the swollen war-time oil price easing off rather than anything wrong at the company — its profits look big right now because fighting near Iran has pushed oil well above the ordinary level Chevron actually plans around.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow has been hit hard, down sharply from its high, even though big companies and government agencies keep signing on for its workflow and AI tools — the fall looks more like market mood than anything broken in the business.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore dropped a bit even as copper prices rose, which is a little odd since they mine copper — the two usually move together, so this looks like the stock lagging behind the metal rather than a problem at the company.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta rose a touch, and the key point is the price it gets per ton of crushed stone is still climbing a healthy few percent — the reported average price looks like it fell only because of what mix of products sold, not because pricing actually weakened.

KOF.sentence: Coca-Cola FEMSA ticked up, but the main drag for US investors is the Mexican peso weakening, since most of its sales are in pesos that are worth fewer dollars when converted.

UBER.sentence: Uber rose again, with people booking more rides and food orders than ever — the open question is still whether self-driving-car companies put their cars on Uber's app or go it alone, but that's a worry about the future, not today's business.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk is trading below what its fleet of ships would cost to replace, which has historically been a solid floor for the stock — the shipping giant is quiet, with global trade steady.

MA.sentence: Mastercard jumped a bit, and notably it's now priced almost even with Visa rather than at its usual premium — nothing is broken at the company, people keep tapping their cards more than ever.

ISRG.sentence: The surgical robot company is down about 28% from its high even though hospitals are still on track to do 13–15% more procedures with its machines — that's a wide gap between the fear in the stock and what's actually happening in operating rooms.

NVDA.sentence: Nvidia dipped as its biggest customers — Google's parent and Amazon — showed they're now spending more on computing gear than their businesses bring in and borrowing the difference, which is the real question hanging over it: not whether Nvidia's chips are good, but whether those few giant buyers can keep paying.
